huge
Shipped the Chrome extension. Popup shows the real daily cap. Drafts for DMs, replies, and comments stay on the page. They never hit the scout queue. Two jobs. One list was making both worse.

Reddit AI moderation just changed who gets to post. It reads comment intent now, not karma. Account age will not save a pitch. We draft the reply and wait for your approve. Auto-post just got riskier.
Distribution is gold

Cut X scout cost ~90% this week. We were re-searching the same posts every hour like they were new threads. Map once. Draft only if it's new. You still approve before anything posts. Paying twice for the same conversation is not growth.
Moved our LLM calls off Opus/Sonnet onto Grok 4.6. Same approve-before-post. We were using the expensive model out of habit. Comments do not need a research paper budget.

Send failures on link approve were coming back as 500, and Cloudflare stripped the body before you saw it. So "why did that fail" was unanswerable. Now it's a 409 with the real reason, and the queue refreshes even when the send dies. An approve gate you can't debug isn't a gate.

The OP usually isn't your buyer. He picks something that afternoon. Your buyer is whoever lands on that thread from Google six months later and reads the top comment.

Which is why the draft has to still help if you delete the Viewfy line. Pitches expire. Answers keep working.

Found the free Arctic Shift archive this week, so discovery hits it before Apify ever bills us. Same threads, one search API call to confirm they're still live. Paid scraping is now the fallback, not the front door. Cheaper discovery means we can scan wider and skip more.

Onboarding had a hardcoded three minute countdown on the Reddit scan. Theater: sometimes done in 40s, sometimes still running at 3:00 and we handed you an empty thread list anyway. Now the step waits on the actual scan. Fake progress bars just teach you to distrust the real ones.

Someone taps approve on a Reddit card they already approved two hours ago, from a stale tab. That used to throw an error and look broken. Now it's a quiet no-op: already decided, nothing double-posts. An approve gate is only trustworthy if the taps are idempotent.

The honest version of "marketing while building": you don't do it in blocks of time, you do it in 90-second decisions. Open the queue, approve three Reddit replies, merge an SEO PR, close the tab. The work still happens. It just stops competing with your commits.
Added a cap on pending drafts, alongside the daily rate. If 12 replies are already sitting unapproved, scouting a 13th thread helps nobody. The queue was outrunning

Watching what founders actually approve, the deciding factor isn't the writing. It's thread age. Under a few hours old: approved. A day old: skipped, because 40 comments already said it. So the hard part was never drafting. It's latency. We optimize for minutes to draft now.

Scanned 156 Show HN launches from last month. 23 block Anthropic's crawler. Zero block OpenAI. Almost half the Cloudflare-hosted ones are unreadable to AI engines entirely. Nobody chose that. They pasted a config file from a template and shipped. Write-up on the blog.

Capped our draft Reddit replies at 2-5 sentences this week. The long ones always read like a pitch wearing a helpful hat: three paragraphs nobody asked for, then the link. Short answers get upvoted. And say you built the thing in the first line, not the last.

Cut Apify out of our Reddit search this week. Paying per scrape to find threads we might not even reply to made no sense. Now it's official Reddit search first, fallbacks chained behind it, so one rate limit doesn't kill discovery. Cheaper and it fails softer.

Dropped blog cadence from daily to every three days. Daily was filling a quota, not a gap. The blog exists so a Reddit reply has something real to point at. If a post can't survive that job, publishing it is just noise. Fewer posts, each one carries its weight.

Our pricing page said the first post is free. The code quietly disagreed. Found it this week and fixed the order: draft, publish, then ask about a plan. The pricing page is the spec now, not the marketing. First post free, no card, like it already claimed.

Compared startup user acquisition tools by the number nobody puts on a pricing page: setup cost. Most want a week of config before the first post exists. So we ranked by channel coverage, workflow fit, and days to first output. Ours: connect the repo, first post free, no card.

A manual SEO audit misses about 40% of technical issues, not because the auditor is lazy but because nobody clicks 400 pages. Automation catches those. It also wants to do things it shouldn't: rewrite your h1 voice, move routes, inject scripts. Wrote up what belongs in a fix PR.

Best part of marketing living in git: it has a history. Someone rewrote your title tags in March, you can see the diff, the author, the reason. Don't like it? git revert. Try that with a dashboard that just says "applied." New post on GitHub marketing integrations is up.

Fixed a dumb loop this week: you close a fix PR, the next audit opens the same one again. Now a rejection sticks. Also, if a diff was never build-checked, the report says so instead of quietly implying green. Saying no should cost you one review, not every week.

Every marketing tool we tried ended in a task list. Dashboard says fix your titles, you still open the editor. So we made the output a diff. Review it where you review everything else, then merge or close. Wrote up marketing automation that fits git. On the blog.

An agency sends you a deck and a list of fixes. You still open the editor. That is the whole gap. Wrote up when an agency is actually the right call (brand, big budgets, human relationships) and when a growth agent is: daily blog, SEO fixes as a PR, X and Threads, Meta ads.

Locked blog categories to the plan clusters this week. The generator kept inventing synonyms: "AI visibility", "LLM visibility", "GEO", three buckets for one topic. Now it picks from the plan or it fails. Fewer categories, more internal links that actually point somewhere.

Shipped agent inbox attach this week. You connect Cloudflare, Viewfy wires hi@inbox.yourdomain, and your agent starts handling inbound from its own address. No ESP setup, no DNS guessing. One OAuth click and it's live.

Later helps you schedule posts. It does not write them, fix your SEO, or run your ads. Viewfy does all four. Daily blog, PRs on your repo, X and Threads posts, managed Meta ads. First post free, no card.

Most founders treat SEO as a checklist. Fix titles, add meta descriptions, done. But the real gap in 2025 is whether AI models can even parse your site. We scanned 383 Show HN launches. 27% were unreadable. If Claude can't read you, Claude can't recommend you.
Shipped async repo briefing on GitHub connect. When you link your repo, Claude reads your codebase before the first audit runs. Fixes land with context, not guesses. No onboarding call needed.

Shipped a cross-channel signup system this week. Viewfy now fills every profile field on every platform before it starts engaging. Reddit gets a brand-shaped username. Threads gets the right bio. No half-built profiles floating around making your product look abandoned.

Hootsuite schedules your social posts. Viewfy writes the blog, opens SEO fixes as a PR on your repo, and runs your ads. One manages a calendar. The other does the marketing work you keep putting off. Comparison is on our blog.
Excited for the cloud future 💙

Shipped a Telegram onboard flow this week. New users link their account, the agent welcomes them back, and messages get stored per-user. No manual setup on your end. Your agent just shows up where your users already are.

Shipped uploadable avatars for agent inboxes this week. Small thing but it matters. When your agent replies in Telegram or handles a signup, it looks like your brand, not a default placeholder. Details like that build trust before anyone clicks through.
Buffer queues your tweets. Viewfy opens a pull request with the blog post, the SEO fixes, and the ad creative. One tool fills a calendar. The other fills a funnel. Full comparison on our blog.

We wrote a blog comparing every option a founder has for growth, agencies, freelancers, SEO tools, social schedulers, and us. No affiliate links. Just scope, output, and how much of your week each one actually takes. Link on our profile.

We published a comparison of Viewfy alternatives for startup growth. No affiliate links, no ranking tricks. Just what each tool actually does and where it falls short. If you're evaluating options, the breakdown is on our blog.

Redesigned the landing page. No more step list, no wizard. Just one glowing URL field and the whole pitch upfront. If you can't explain it in one screen, you're overcomplicating it. Ship notes from today.
